title_masked: Bidirectional serial replication will block if a region’s last edit before rs crashed was from the peer cluster
A_explanation: The replication blocks because the system cannot determine that edits 59-60 have been pushed. SerialReplicationChecker.pushed.load fails to load the persisted last sequence ID, resetting it to NO_SEQNUM. Consequently, SerialReplicationChecker.isRangeFinished incorrectly determines the range is not finished because pushedSeqId is reset. SerialReplicationChecker.canPush logs 'Previous range ... not finished' (L2) and blocks. SerialReplicationChecker.waitUntilCanPush then spins in a wait loop (L3) because SerialReplicationChecker.canPush prevents progress. The root cause is the failure to restore state in SerialReplicationChecker.pushed.load.
B_explanation: The replication source (SerialReplicationSourceWALReader.readWALEntries) triggers SerialReplicationChecker.waitUntilCanPush to wait because SerialReplicationChecker.canPush's canPush returns false (L1, L2). This stems from SerialReplicationChecker.isRangeFinished's isRangeFinished, which checks if the last pushed sequence ID has reached the barrier. In bidirectional serial replication, if the last edit before a crash was from the peer, the local 'last pushed' ID does not advance for those peer-received edits. Consequently, SerialReplicationChecker.isRangeFinished incorrectly reports the range as unfinished, causing SerialReplicationChecker.canPush to log 'give up' (L2) and SerialReplicationChecker.waitUntilCanPush to log 'wait' (L3) indefinitely.
